title: Taking over Joe's cornet chair and the first audition
summary: After Joe left he sat in a few times, was encouraged by John Chaff to keep practicing, and recalls first hearing the Straws as the most original band in the city.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Let's see now. So, you came back and you didn't play with the straws again at all until May or so?

Uh, well, I, I think maybe I sat in twice with them playing trombone. One time I played, uh, I played the cornet. I played second cornet. Joe was playing first. And I, we tried to work up, uh, Oliver Armstrong get up, you see, with the first and second cornets. And, uh, well, after Joe left, well, of course, I had some big shoes to walk into, because, uh, Joe, I thought Joe, I tried to copy Joe's style. I think Joe was terrific. I mean, other people might have a different idea, you know, a different opinion of what they, what they would like to hear. But I thought Joe's stuff was great. Of course, his horn was always flat, but he was good. Could be, too, that vintage of horn he had. I think it was the first horn I'd ever made.
Yeah. When did you, uh, start playing spots with the straws?
Well, I guess, uh, it must have been about May. I think, uh, we had two jobs, uh, right, right after Joe left. We had these two jobs, and, uh, I played both of those.
What I mean is, you never substituted for Joe before he left.
He always made all the jobs.

He always made all the jobs, yeah, unfortunately. Because I didn't want to get in and play, you know, more than I actually did. But, uh, I would go and listen to him, you know. I'd go up to Bruno's and listen to him play. And, uh, uh, uh, Briss, Briss Jones, the clarinetist, he played with this, uh, group we had up in Kenna years ago. You know, he sat in with us a couple of times. And, uh, he told John Chaff, he told John, he says, uh, he said, well, you know, Moose plays a con-ed. So, John asked me if I would like to sit in and play a tune with him, see. So, uh, oh, I think, uh, I think we played Hauna Society. And, uh, Bill Bailey, Milenburg, George. And, uh, John was pretty much pleased with the sound, you know. So, uh, he told me, he says, uh, you should keep practicing that horn, keep working on it, because Joe is going to be leaving us permanently. And, uh, we got to fill in, he says, and, uh, you know, the style of stuff you play is pretty much the same style that Joe plays. So, you know, you keep working with the horn and we'll have a spot for you in the groove. Well, I remember the first time I'd ever heard the Straws play, uh, it was at one of the jazz club meetings, uh, concerts, rather. And I told these fellas that I was with, I said, as far as I'm concerned, that's undoubtedly the most original sounding band in this city, bar none. He says, never dreamed that I'd ever have a chance to play with him, you know. And, uh, it all worked out.
Well, what do you play at other than Bruno's? What other places?
